column7: What, if anything, has changed in your life since you started at the garden?
column8: What would make the garden better for you?

column7: I’ve made friends I would never have met otherwise, people of all ages. I’m outside more and I sleep better. My children now eat vegetables they used to refuse, because they grew them.
column8: Clearer rules about shared tools. Things go missing from the shed and nobody knows who is responsible.

column7: Not much has changed, to be honest, I’ve been doing this for years. It keeps me fit and out of the pub.
column8: Get the council to fix the fences. We’ve had three break-ins this year.

column7: I moved here for work and didn’t know anyone. The Wednesday volunteer session became my anchor. My anxiety is much easier to manage when I have my hands in soil.
column8: More sessions in the evening for people who work. And less paperwork to become a volunteer: it took me two months.

column7: Since my husband went into a care home, the garden is where I see people. Some weeks it is the only conversation I have.
column8: A toilet! And a few more benches in the shade.

column7: I eat seasonally now and waste far less. I understand where food comes from, and so do my neighbours’ children.
column8: More hands. The same five people do all the work, and we are tired.
